avoid.reason: Clifton Hill's tourist strip has inflated prices and occasional aggressive touts; watch belongings in peak-season crowds.

hood_desc: The carnival-bright entertainment strip of arcades, wax museums, and mini-golf a short walk from the Falls; suits families and first-time visitors wanting everything within stumbling distance.
The high-rise hotel and casino district with the best direct Falls views from guest rooms and restaurants; suits travelers prioritizing the view over budget.
A quieter revitalizing downtown with antique shops, cafes, and the VIA Rail station, a short drive or bus ride from the Falls themselves.
A historic riverside village upstream from the Falls with War of 1812 heritage sites and a slower pace; suits those wanting to escape the tourist crowds.
A green, walkable stretch of parkland and gardens along the upper river, good for cycling and a break from the casino strip.

food.name: Peameal bacon sandwich
food.desc: Canada's own back bacon, brined and rolled in cornmeal, griddled thick and stacked on a soft kaiser roll with mustard. A southern Ontario breakfast staple.

places.name: Taps Brewhouse
places.note: Weekend brunch menu leans hard into Canadian classics, with house beer alongside.

places.name: The Flour Mill Scratch Kitchen
places.note: Everything made in-house in the downtown heritage district; strong all-day breakfast.

food.name: Poutine
food.desc: Hot fries, squeaky cheese curds and gravy poured over the top so the curds just begin to melt. Ontario piles on everything from smoked meat to butter chicken.

places.name: Smoke's Poutinerie
places.note: Canadian chain with a long list of loaded versions; open late on the tourist strip.

places.name: Taps Brewhouse
places.note: Several poutine variations to pair with locally brewed beer.

places.name: BeaverTails
places.note: Serves poutine and fries alongside the pastries if you want both in one stop.

food.name: Butter tart
food.desc: A flaky pastry shell filled with butter, sugar and egg, baked until the centre is somewhere between gooey and set. Ontario argues endlessly about raisins.

places.name: The Sweet Oven
places.note: Butter tart specialist with a rotating wall of flavours, from classic to maple bacon.

places.name: Willow Cakes and Pastries
places.note: Old-town bakery worth the short drive; good stop on a winery day.

food.name: BeaverTails
food.desc: Hand-stretched whole wheat dough fried into a flat oval and served hot with cinnamon sugar, chocolate hazelnut or maple butter. A Canadian tourist rite.

places.name: BeaverTails Clifton Hill
places.note: Beside Ripley's Moving Theatre in the middle of the arcade strip; open late.

places.name: BeaverTails Table Rock
places.note: Closest location to the brink of the Horseshoe Falls, so you can eat it with the view.

food.name: Niagara farm-to-table
food.desc: The peninsula's peaches, cherries, tender fruit and Lake Erie fish, cooked simply and matched to VQA wine grown in the same fields.

places.name: Treadwell Cuisine
places.note: The region's most decorated restaurant; huge VQA cellar and a seasonal Niagara-grown menu.

places.name: Trius Winery Restaurant
places.note: Vineyard dining with dishes built around the estate's own wines.

places.name: Table Rock House Restaurant
places.note: Local ingredients and the closest dining room to the Horseshoe Falls; book ahead.

food.name: Icewine
food.desc: Grapes left to freeze on the vine to about minus 8C, then pressed for a tiny amount of intensely sweet juice. Niagara is the world's largest producer.

places.name: Inniskillin
places.note: Pioneered Canadian icewine in the 1980s; tastings pair it with cheese and chocolate.

places.name: Peller Estates
places.note: The 10Below Icewine Lounge is a minus 10C ice room where you taste in a parka.

places.name: Lakeview Wine Co.
places.note: Ice flight tastings that let you compare several styles side by side.

food.name: Niagara craft beer
food.desc: The wine region also brews well, with lagers, hoppy ales and small-batch experiments including beers made with icewine grapes.

places.name: Niagara College Teaching Brewery
places.note: Student-run brewery and winery on a working campus; tours end in a tasting.

places.name: Silversmith Brewing Company
places.note: Brewed inside a converted 1894 church; the Black Lager is the flagship.

places.name: Taps Brewhouse
places.note: Niagara Falls' own brewpub, the easiest option without leaving town.

landmarks: Horseshoe Falls
The mightiest of Niagara's cataracts thunders 57 meters in a vast emerald curve, drenching onlookers in mist on the Canadian brink.
Journey Behind the Falls
Elevators descend through bedrock to tunnels and an observation deck directly beside and behind the roaring curtain of Horseshoe Falls.
Niagara City Cruises (Voyage to the Falls)
The iconic red-ponchoed catamaran sails straight into the Horseshoe's misty basin, the most exhilarating way to feel the falls' power.
Skylon Tower
A 236-meter observation tower whose yellow bugs climb the exterior to revolving-restaurant views spanning both falls and the Niagara skyline.
Table Rock and Queen Victoria Park
Manicured Victorian gardens run along the gorge rim to Table Rock's railing, the closest free viewpoint at the Horseshoe's very edge.
Clifton Hill
Niagara's gloriously kitschy 'Street of Fun' tumbles toward the falls with a giant SkyWheel, wax museums, arcades and neon by night.
Whirlpool Aero Car
A 1916 Spanish-designed cable car glides above the swirling Niagara Whirlpool, where the rapids make a violent ninety-degree turn.
White Water Walk
A boardwalk at the gorge bottom skirts Class 6 rapids, some of the wildest white water in North America.
Niagara Parks Butterfly Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
Two thousand free-flying butterflies flutter through a rainforest dome set within ninety-nine acres of immaculate botanical gardens north of the falls.
Niagara-on-the-Lake
A twenty-minute river drive ends in Canada's prettiest Victorian town, wrapped in wineries, flower baskets and the historic Fort George.

intl.to: New York City (USA) via Buffalo & Albany

train.note: Niagara Falls is one of the few Canadian cities with a genuine international train: Amtrak's Maple Leaf runs daily from Niagara Falls ON through Buffalo and Albany to New York City in about 11 hours, operated jointly with VIA Rail on the Canadian side. Border formalities are done at the Niagara Falls station stop and can take an hour or more, so carry your passport. VIA and GO Transit trains run to Toronto in about 2 hours, with GO's seasonal weekend service the cheaper option.

bus.note: Cross-border coaches use the Rainbow or Peace Bridge, where everyone gets off for US immigration - allow an hour and carry your passport and any required visa or ESTA. Megabus and FlixBus run frequently to Toronto in about 90 minutes from the bus terminal beside the train station. The WEGO bus network covers the falls, Clifton Hill and Niagara-on-the-Lake locally.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry at Niagara Falls - the river above and below the falls is far too dangerous. The Maid of the Mist and Niagara City Cruises boats that run into the spray are sightseeing excursions, not transport, and operate roughly April to November. All crossings to the United States here are by road or rail bridge.

half.name: Niagara Falls, USA
half.blurb: Crossing the Rainbow Bridge reveals the American and Bridal Veil Falls from Niagara Falls State Park on the U.S. side.

half.name: Buffalo
half.blurb: Frank Lloyd Wright's Darwin Martin House and a revived Lake Erie waterfront sit about thirty minutes across the border.

half.name: Hamilton
half.blurb: Royal Botanical Gardens and the Dundas Peak escarpment lookout are roughly forty-five minutes from the falls.

half.name: St. Catharines
half.blurb: Twenty Valley wineries and the Welland Canal shipping locks lie about twenty minutes from Niagara Falls.

notes.walk: Central Fallsview and Clifton Hill are very walkable along the Falls; reaching Niagara-on-the-Lake wineries or Chippawa requires a car, bus, or WEGO shuttle
notes.card: Widely accepted everywhere, including tap-to-pay; cash mainly useful for small vendors
notes.safety: Very safe, well-patrolled tourist zone with heavy foot traffic day and night. Petty tourist scams and overpriced attractions are the main risk, not violent crime.
notes.religion: Christianity (Roman Catholic and Protestant majority); no religious affiliation (growing share)
notes.langs: English; French (official Canadian second language, limited local use)
notes.net: Strong 4G/5G coverage throughout. Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes. ~$30-45 for a 10GB prepaid tourist SIM. Free wifi widely available. A Canadian prepaid SIM or eSIM from Rogers/Bell/Telus.
notes.transit: WEGO shuttle buses linking hotels, attractions, and the Falls; Niagara Region Transit for wider area
notes.transport: Toronto Pearson International (YYZ), about 1.5 hr; Buffalo Niagara International (BUF, USA) is closer at 25-30 min. VIA Rail station with service to Toronto and connections onward. GO Transit and Megabus connect to Toronto and other Ontario cities. Easy via the QEW highway from Toronto; parking at Falls-area lots and garages.
